This is the help of `rusticdoc 0.1.0`. The CLI is the same binary as the service. See [Install](/docs/start/install/) for how to run it.

## rusticdoc

```text
Templates in, documents out. Run `serve` for the HTTP API.

Usage: rusticdoc [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  render          Fill a template and run the steps, writing one file
  convert         Convert one or more documents
  serve           Run the HTTP service. Settings come from RUSTICDOC_* variables
  openapi         Print the OpenAPI description as JSON
  health          Check a running service, for container health checks. Exits 0 when up
  engines         Show the engines this machine has
  pdf             PDF operations: merge, split, rotate, flatten, optimize, encrypt, metadata, bookmarks, embed, watermark, stamp, factur-x, forms
  validate        Check a template against sample data and list every problem
  webhook-secret  Print the key a caller's webhook deliveries are signed with, in hex, from RUSTICDOC_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A receiver decodes it and verifies with it
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...  Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
  -h, --help        Print help
  -V, --version     Print version
```

### rusticdoc render

```text
Fill a template and run the steps, writing one file

Usage: rusticdoc render [OPTIONS] <TEMPLATE>

Arguments:
  <TEMPLATE>  The template file

Options:
  -d, --data <DATA>
          JSON file with the data the template sees
  -v, --verbose...
          Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --ctx <CTX>
          JSON file visible as `ctx`
  -s, --steps <STEPS>
          Steps in order: convert, pdfa, metadata, encrypt, merge [default: ""]
      --to <TO>
          Output format for `convert` [default: pdf]
      --pdfa <PDFA>
          PDF/A level for `pdfa` [default: PDF/A-2b]
      --metadata <METADATA>
          JSON object for `metadata`
      --user-password <USER_PASSWORD>
          
      --owner-password <OWNER_PASSWORD>
          
      --merge-with <MERGE_WITH>
          Extra PDFs for `merge`
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Where to write the result. Defaults to the template's name with the output extension
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### rusticdoc convert

```text
Convert one or more documents

Usage: rusticdoc convert [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...  Documents to convert

Options:
      --to <TO>          [default: pdf]
  -v, --verbose...       Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --pdfa <PDFA>      Export PDF/A at this level instead of plain PDF
      --merge            Merge all inputs into one PDF
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  Output file (one input or --merge), or directory (several inputs)
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### rusticdoc pdf

```text
PDF operations: merge, split, rotate, flatten, optimize, encrypt, metadata, bookmarks, embed, watermark, stamp, factur-x, forms

Usage: rusticdoc pdf [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  merge      Merge PDFs in the order given
  split      Split by page ranges (`1-3,5`) or into intervals of N pages
  rotate     Rotate pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees
  flatten    Flatten forms and annotations into the page content
  optimize   Recompress streams and drop unused objects
  encrypt    Encrypt with AES-256
  metadata   Read metadata as JSON, or write keys from a JSON object
  bookmarks  Read the outline as JSON, or replace it from a JSON array
  embed      Attach files to a PDF
  watermark  Put text, an image or a PDF under the page content
  stamp      Put text, an image or a PDF over the page content
  sign       Place a signature image at exact coordinates (not a cryptographic signature)
  facturx    Embed Factur-X invoice XML
  fields     List a form's fields as JSON
  fill       Fill a form from JSON data; tags in annotations are applied too
  overlay    Lay one PDF over another, page by page
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...  Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
  -h, --help        Print help
```

#### rusticdoc pdf merge

```text
Merge PDFs in the order given

Usage: rusticdoc pdf merge [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...  

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  
  -v, --verbose...       Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
  -h, --help             Print help
```

#### rusticdoc pdf split

```text
Split by page ranges (`1-3,5`) or into intervals of N pages

Usage: rusticdoc pdf split [OPTIONS] --span <SPAN> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>  

Options:
      --mode <MODE>      `pages` or `intervals` [default: pages]
  -v, --verbose...       Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --span <SPAN>      Ranges for `pages`, a page count for `intervals`
      --unify            One file holding every range instead of one per range
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  Directory for the parts [default: .]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

#### rusticdoc pdf rotate

```text
Rotate pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees

Usage: rusticdoc pdf rotate [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>  

Options:
      --angle <ANGLE>    [default: 90]
  -v, --verbose...       Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --pages <PAGES>    Page selection such as `1-3,5`; all when empty [default: ""]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  
  -h, --help             Print help
```

#### rusticdoc pdf watermark

```text
Put text, an image or a PDF under the page content

Usage: rusticdoc pdf watermark [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>  

Options:
      --text <TEXT>            Text for a text mark
  -v, --verbose...             Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --mark <MARK_FILE>       PNG, JPEG or PDF file for an image or PDF mark
      --position <POSITION>    top-left, top-center, top-right, center, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right [default: center]
      --opacity <OPACITY>      [default: 1]
      --rotation <ROTATION>    [default: 0]
      --scale <SCALE>          Relative to the page width, 0 to 1 [default: 0.5]
      --font-size <FONT_SIZE>  [default: 24]
      --colour <COLOUR>        [default: #808080]
      --pages <PAGES>          [default: ""]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>        
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

#### rusticdoc pdf sign

```text
Place a signature image at exact coordinates (not a cryptographic signature)

Usage: rusticdoc pdf sign [OPTIONS] --image <IMAGE> --x <X> --y <Y> --output <OUTPUT> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>  

Options:
      --image <IMAGE>    PNG or JPEG
  -v, --verbose...       Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --page <PAGE>      [default: 1]
      --x <X>            Points from the page's left edge
      --y <Y>            Points from the page's bottom edge
      --width <WIDTH>    Width in points; default the image's natural size
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### rusticdoc webhook-secret

```text
Print the key a caller's webhook deliveries are signed with, in hex, from RUSTICDOC_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A receiver decodes it and verifies with it

Usage: rusticdoc webhook-secret [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --api-key <API_KEY>            The caller's API key
  -v, --verbose...                   Log verbosity: -v for debug, -vv for trace
      --basic-user <BASIC_USER>      The caller's basic-auth user
      --oidc-subject <OIDC_SUBJECT>  The subject of the caller's OpenID Connect tokens

```
